record.file_problem: This is a repository record containing metadata, README text, and a file list only. The code and other listed documents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README uses an Arditi-style refusal-direction projection as part of a transparency tool and reports probe measurements, but does not test whether removing or adding the direction changes refusal or capability.
record.gate_note: The README reports projection and probe-separation measurements. These are recorded as findings about the measured direction, but they do not test the causal or behavioral effects named by the claim versions. The README also describes scripts and analyses without reporting their outcomes; those descriptions are not results.
record.test_reason: ESTA is a tool repository. It extracts an Arditi-style difference-in-means refusal direction and uses its projection as a 'safety pressure' readout. It reports only probe and projection separation on Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct. No ablation, addition, weight edit, attack, transfer or training comparison is reported, so its results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README presents the refusal-direction projection as an auditable safety-pressure signal that cleanly separates refused from answered prompts on Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct (AUC 1.00). It makes no claim about causal removal or addition.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repository. It says extraction follows Arditi et al. (2024), and reports a layer-14 projection probe; it does not report the original ablation or addition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports a large difference between the built-in smoke-test prompts on Qwen 2.5 0.5B (separation 0.51) and held-out AdvBench/Alpaca prompts on Qwen 2.5 7B (22.89).

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct at layer 14, the projection onto the difference-in-means direction separates harmless prompts from refused prompts completely: harmless projections reach at most 11.06, refusals start at 15.10, and AUC is 1.00. Class means rise from factual (3.4) to how-to (8.7) to defensive (11.6) to refused (27.6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projection onto the refusal direction is a correlational readout that separates refused from answered prompts in Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct.

fits_no_version.finding: The quality of the extracted direction depends strongly on the prompt sets and model. Built-in prompts on the 0.5B model give a separation of 0.51, against 22.89 for 200 AdvBench vs 200 Alpaca prompts on the 7B model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How cleanly the refusal direction is extracted depends on the size and matching of the prompt sets.

record.problems: The README provides no uncertainty estimates for the reported probe measurements and no causal intervention or capability test. The numbers are README-reported results; the code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No reported README measurements relevant to the refusal-direction projection were left out. Script descriptions without reported outcomes were not recorded as results.

untested.parts: Ablating the direction, adding it, and checking other capabilities are all untested.
No weight edit or abliteration is reported.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training against the direction is reported.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis is reported.
Harmfulness and refusal are not separated. The dual-use script that would probe topic versus refusal is described, but its outcome is not reported in the README.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of training methods or stages is reported.

missing.what: Results of the dual-use analysis (defensive vs offensive prompt pairs, matched-control AUCs, behavioural over-refusal), which would bear on whether the direction tracks topic or refusal disposition (loosely V5). The script is described, but its results are not in the README text.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was available. The research site and design docs may hold further probe results, such as dual-use and framing analyses. None of the README results is an intervention, so no verdicts are given. The 92%→14% elevated-label figures are threshold-policy choices of the tool and are rightly not recorded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or addition is reported; refusal behavior after intervention and other capabilities are not measured.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No attack that suppresses the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
No test of an affine, cone, or multi-direction account is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.
